text:
anna_support: Hey team — customer running a content editing flow reporting a sharp spike in 429s when users hit "regen" after making edits. They do a small embed prefetch + 4 parallel regen calls. Seeing 429s on regen only, embeddings mostly succeed. Logs attached below.

anna_support: key log snippet: 
```
2026-02-14T15:12:03Z frontend: POST /v1/regenerate  -> 429, headers: Retry-After: 1, X-RateLimit-Limit-PerModel: 1200, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-Model-Concurrency-Limit: 6
2026-02-14T15:12:03Z frontend: POST /v1/embeds -> 200, latency 220ms
```

jordan_sre: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl or script) and say which model variants they're hitting? need to check fanout + token-per-request math.

anna_support: Repro in prod lowered to 1 user: they sequentially do: 1) prefetch embeddings -> 2) trigger 4 parallel regenerations (same prompt, different temperature). Models: rwd-32k (3 requests) + rwd-64k (1 request). Each regen is ~8k tokens total. They see 3/4 regen requests return 429 within ~100ms of the first success.

sam_engineer: This looks like a "regen storm" + mixed-variant fanout. Two things compounding: per-model token-rate (RPM/TPM) and per-instance concurrency cap. 64k variants typically have lower concurrent slots, and token accounting can cause the token-bucket to hit zero when multiple large requests start near-simultaneously.

sam_engineer: Quick checklist: 1) confirm token accounting headers on failing responses (X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset). 2) check whether the requests are hitting the same customer route/model cluster (fan-in). 3) validate client retry/backoff.

mika_prod: Customer attached the failing response headers in the UI: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
X-RateLimit-Limit-PerModel: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Window: 60s
X-Model-Concurrency-Limit: 6
X-Model-Concurrency-Used: 5
```

mika_prod: They also saw a transient 401 on one embed call during the same window — likely independent token refresh flake.

jordan_sre: Good. Two guidance items for the customer: reduce parallel regenerations (serialize or cap), and add jittered exponential backoff with max retries. Also recommend grouping prefetch so it's not done at the exact same time as regen fanout.

sam_engineer: Concrete settings we can suggest (from platform best-practices):
- Limit parallel regenerations per user to 2-3 concurrent requests.
- For large-context variants (>= 32k) set a lower concurrency cap on client side (max_concurrency: 3).
- Backoff policy: initial 300ms, factor 2, jitter +/-100ms, max delay 5s, max attempts 6.

sam_engineer: Example pseudo-snippet for client throttle: 
```
// simple token-bucket + concurrency guard
const MAX_CONCURRENCY = 3; // per-user cap for regen on big models
const semaphore = new Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENCY);
await semaphore.acquire();
try {
  await callRegenerate();
} finally {
  semaphore.release();
}
```

anna_support: Customer asked whether this is "per-account" or "per-model" limit — they have heavy usage on rwd-32k but occasional 64k fallbacks.

sam_engineer: Limits are multi-dimensional: there's a per-model RPM/TPM token bucket and a concurrency cap on the serving side for each model variant. When you hit either, you get throttled. With mixed fanout you can exhaust the per-model token budget faster even if individual model concurrency is not saturated.

sam_engineer: If they need higher sustained regeneration throughput, options: 1) request a higher reserved capacity for the affected model variant (Dedicated capacity), 2) reduce per-request token usage (trim context), 3) shard requests over time (stagger parallelism).

jordan_sre: For support reproduction, here's a small k6 snippet to simulate the pattern (replace URL/KEY):
```
import http from 'k6/http';
export default function () {
  // prefetch
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeds', { /* body */ }, { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer $KEY' } });
  // launch 4 parallel regen (approx):
  const reqs = new Array(4).fill(0).map(_ => http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/regenerate', { /* body */ }));
}
```

mika_prod: I recommended the customer temporarily lower their parallelism from 4 -> 2 and enable backoff. They did that and reported regen 429s dropped to near zero during a 24h test. They still want to avoid changing UX.

sam_engineer: Another handle: implement a cheap preflight check against rate headers before firing heavy requests. Example: call a low-cost /v1/health or rate-preview endpoint that returns remaining tokens for that model/route and gate the regen storm if remaining < threshold.

anna_support: They asked about Token Billing spikes — will failed 429s count toward billing?

mika_prod: 429s do not bill for consumed tokens beyond what was accepted by the server; partial token accounting can vary with early rejection, but generally embed calls that succeed bill; regen requests that are rejected do not consume token quota. If they see billing anomalies, open a ticket with usage logs.

jordan_sre: Follow-up action: support to provide a small replay script + exact failing response headers and a K/V of "concurrency used" values (from logs) so infra can correlate to serving instance queueing. I'll take point on that.

infra-bot: Note: created incident stub #INC-2026-047 for high regen 429 pattern for customer-342.

anna_support: Customer accepted the mitigation plan (limit concurrency + add backoff) and requested a follow-up to discuss Dedicated capacity. I'll schedule a call. Thanks all.

sam_engineer: TL;DR for support doc: regen storms + mixed-variant fanout -> token bucket exhaustion + small concurrency slots on large models. Recommend throttle clients, add backoff, stagger prefetch, or increase dedicated capacity.
